objective: Decide whether n^2 + n + 41 is prime for every non-negative integer n.
intuition: Test the universal primality claim for the Euler polynomial n^2 + n + 41.
success_criteria: Exhibit an integer n for which n^2 + n + 41 is composite.
State the counterexample factorisation exactly.
failure_modes: Check only small n where the value happens to be prime.
Report that the polynomial is 'usually' prime as if that settled the universal claim.

objective: Decide whether the Kretschmann scalar of the Schwarzschild metric vanishes at the horizon r = 2M.
intuition: Test the claim that curvature vanishes at the Schwarzschild horizon.
success_criteria: Compute the Kretschmann scalar K = 48 M^2 / r^6 exactly.
Evaluate K at r = 2M and show it is finite and nonzero.
failure_modes: Confuse the coordinate singularity of the metric component with a curvature singularity.
Conclude vanishing curvature from g_tt -> 0 at the horizon.

objective: Decide whether every Ricci-flat spacetime (R_{ab} = 0) is flat (Riemann = 0).
intuition: Test whether vanishing Ricci curvature forces vanishing Riemann curvature.
success_criteria: Exhibit a Ricci-flat metric that is not flat.
Show the Schwarzschild metric has R_{ab} = 0 but a nonzero Weyl/Riemann tensor.
failure_modes: Assume Ricci = 0 implies Riemann = 0 in dimension four.
Ignore the Weyl part of the curvature.

objective: Decide whether the eigenvalues of the Pauli matrix sigma_x are 0 and 1.
intuition: Test the claimed spectrum {0, 1} of sigma_x.
success_criteria: Compute the characteristic polynomial of sigma_x.
Show its eigenvalues are +1 and -1, not 0 and 1.
failure_modes: Confuse the spectrum of sigma_x with that of a projector.
Read eigenvalues off the diagonal of a non-diagonal matrix.

objective: Decide whether the canonical commutator [x, p] equals zero.
intuition: Test the claim that position and momentum commute.
success_criteria: Apply [x, p] to a test function with p = -i hbar d/dx.
Show [x, p] = i hbar, not 0.
failure_modes: Treat x and p as commuting c-numbers.
Drop the derivative acting on the product x*psi.

objective: Decide whether the volumetric flow rate in Hagen-Poiseuille pipe flow scales linearly with the pipe radius, Q proportional to R.
intuition: Test the radius scaling of laminar volumetric flow rate.
success_criteria: Derive Q = pi R^4 (dP/dx) / (8 mu) from the parabolic profile.
Show Q scales as R^4, not R.
failure_modes: Confuse the cross-sectional area scaling (R^2) or the mean velocity with the full flow-rate scaling.
Assume flow rate is proportional to radius by analogy with circumference.

objective: Decide whether the Reynolds number Re = rho v L / mu carries dimensions of velocity.
intuition: Test the dimensional character of the Reynolds number.
success_criteria: Reduce the dimensions of rho v L / mu.
Show the result is dimensionless, not a velocity.
failure_modes: Cancel dimensions incorrectly and retain a spurious length or time.
Assume any group containing v inherits a velocity dimension.

objective: Decide whether the equilibrium x = 0 of the logistic equation x' = x(1 - x) is asymptotically stable.
intuition: Test the stability of the origin for the logistic flow.
success_criteria: Linearise: f'(x) = 1 - 2x, so f'(0) = 1 > 0.
Conclude x = 0 is unstable; x = 1 is the stable equilibrium.
failure_modes: Confuse the two equilibria x = 0 and x = 1.
Infer stability from x = 0 being a fixed point alone.

objective: Decide whether the harmonic series sum_{n=1}^infinity 1/n converges.
intuition: Test convergence of the harmonic series.
success_criteria: Apply the Cauchy condensation or 2^k block-grouping argument.
Show the partial sums exceed any bound, so the series diverges.
failure_modes: Infer convergence from the terms 1/n tending to zero.
Treat a large finite partial sum as evidence of a finite limit.

objective: Decide whether a real symmetric matrix can have a non-real (complex) eigenvalue.
intuition: Test whether real symmetry permits complex eigenvalues.
success_criteria: Use the spectral theorem: a real symmetric matrix is orthogonally diagonalisable with real eigenvalues.
Conclude every eigenvalue is real, refuting the claim.
failure_modes: Confuse real symmetric with general real (non-symmetric) matrices, which can have complex eigenvalues.
Offer a non-symmetric rotation matrix as a purported counterexample.
